source.title: Learning Interpretable Features in Audio Latent Spaces via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Nathan Paek; Yong-Yi Zang; Qi-Hui Yang; Randal J. Leistikow

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAEs and feature-to-concept probes in audio-model latent spaces, a new modality for the indirect-evidence version; it does not test toy-model superposition or LLM representations.
record.gate_note: The reported SAE sparsity and probe results bear on whether SAEs recover sparse, interpretable features. The control-vector demonstrations and generation-process analysis do not directly test the claim versions. Grid-search settings are not separate findings.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as an interpretability tool on audio autoencoder latents and reports only how its own pipeline performs: SAE sparsity under its chosen L1 penalties and linear-probe accuracy. No probe is run on the raw latents, no random-feature or chance comparison is given, and nothing is measured about superposition, overlap, polysemanticity or LLMs. The SAE sparsity ratio follows from the L1 coefficient the authors set, so it says nothing about the model's own features.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE features on audio latents 'naturally align with acoustic properties', enabling control-vector manipulation and analysis of how pitch, timbre and loudness emerge during DiffRhythm generation (pitch converges first, loudness last).
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on audio encoder latents and maps their activations to acoustic concepts with linear probes; it does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported sparsity and probe performance vary across audio latent spaces; the study also reports probe accuracy across sparsity levels.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on SAE features trained on audio autoencoder latents decode pitch well (0.75–0.87 across sparsity levels), loudness well only for EnCodec (0.56–0.63), and timbre poorly (0.17–0.46). No raw-latent comparison is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features trained on audio generative-model latents linearly encode acoustic attributes such as pitch.

record.problems: No chance or other baseline for the probe accuracies is stated, and the text reports ranges rather than per-configuration probe results. The study does not test feature overlap, geometry, capacity pressure, or LLM representations.
record.rows_left_out: The control-vector demonstrations in Section 3.1 and generation-progress analysis in Section 3.2 were not included because they do not directly measure a claim version. Figure 4 reports mean and standard deviation for generation progress, but that measure is not about feature recovery or the claim's geometry.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
All: no LLMs, no neuron-level spreading measure, and no evidence that SAE features reflect model features rather than artifacts of the SAE objective.
All: no completeness, stability or canonicality tests across SAEs.
All: feature dimensionality is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests classification is not justified. Superposition appears only as motivation in the introduction. Sparsity ratios are set by λ, and the probe results have no baseline, so no version can be judged. The control-vector and generation-process results were rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric structure.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or importance-dependent feature allocation.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study concerns audio models, not LLMs, and does not measure features spread across neurons. It tests SAE-derived acoustic features in audio latent spaces.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
Whether the underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: DiffRhythm
rows.operation_detail: Measured sparsity ratios of SAE representations across tested configurations.
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Training SAEs on audio latent spaces
rows.note: Range reported across configurations; the text does not give individual configuration results.
rows.check: The sparsity ratio is an outcome of the SAE training choices (λ, hidden size) from a grid search. It is not evidence that the model contains sparse features, so it should not be a V4 row.

rows.subject: WavTokenizer
rows.operation_detail: Measured sparsity ratios of SAE representations across tested configurations.
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Training SAEs on audio latent spaces
rows.note: Range reported across configurations; the text characterizes these as the sparsest representations.
rows.check: Same issue as R1: SAE sparsity set by λ. The authors' remark about tokens being 'highly disentangled' is interpretation, not a measured result.

rows.note: Range reported across configurations; the text does not give individual configuration results.
rows.check: Same issue as R1: SAE sparsity reflects the hyperparameter grid, not the model's representation.

rows.subject: Audio encoder SAEs (aggregate across tested models)
rows.operation_detail: Trained linear probes from SAE features to discretized pitch classes and measured test-set accuracy.
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Training linear probes from SAE features to acoustic concepts; Figure 3
rows.note: The paper reports this range across models and sparsity levels, without per-model values in the text.
rows.check: This is the method's own probe performance. There is no raw-latent or chance baseline, so it cannot show that the SAE recovers features beyond those already linearly present in the latent. The subject is audio codecs/VAEs, not LLMs.
